articles.title: The Colour That Learned to Give Orders
articles.summary: The city first uses red cloth to recognise grain officers; decades later, people obey the colour itself.
articles.summaryZh: 城里最初只用红布认出粮官，几十年后，人们已经开始服从红色本身。
storyParagraphs: After a great fire, relief grain vanished through duplicate claims, and the council had three days to reopen the granary. It told authorised officers to tie red cloth over one shoulder so exhausted guards could recognise them quickly. The choice worked: queues shortened and fewer false claimants reached the scales. At first the cloth was only a marker. Officers still showed written orders, guards checked names, and the red strips were collected each evening in a plain wooden tray.

Years passed. Red appeared on seals, door plaques, chairs, and eventually the collars of officers' children. Traders stepped aside when it approached; clerks closed private ledgers; inns moved red-clad guests to better rooms. New guards had never seen the fire and stopped asking for papers. A temporary shortcut now opened real doors, altered prices, and decided whose complaint was heard first. Those consequences made the colour seem to confirm the distinction it had helped produce.

Tailoring apprentice Xiaoxin discovered this while rushing an officer's repaired coat back before a ceremony. He laid its red strip across his shoulder to keep it from the mud. A guard waved him through, a clerk gave him a storeroom key, and petitioners moved aside. Xiaoxin first protested, then remembered the fine his master faced for being late. He crossed three restricted rooms, delivered the coat early, and kept silent about the key.

A missing grain ledger was blamed on him because witnesses remembered 'a red shoulder' inside. The officer denied lending his status; the guards insisted red had always meant authority. An archivist brought the first fire order from storage: 'Use red cloth temporarily for recognition.' The cloth had no natural power, yet decades of rules, repeated deference, appointments, and punishments had made acting against it costly. Xiaoxin still faced the material danger of accusation even after everyone read the original sentence.

Before reopening, the council tested three gates. At one, guards checked papers; at another, they trusted colour; at the third, officers wore no strip. The same people received different speed, suspicion, and access depending on the rule around the cloth. Rain still spoiled grain and locked doors still stopped bodies, but the hierarchy attached to red changed with collective practice rather than fabric dye. The granary restored document checks and recorded who issued each strip. Some officials objected because the slower gate exposed privileges they had come to treat as ordinary. Xiaoxin lost a week's wages while the ledger was found in another office. When he returned to the shop, he folded the red strip into the wooden tray rather than over his shoulder; outside, people still stepped aside for the next person wearing one.
storyParagraphsZh: 旧城大火后，救济粮不断被人冒名领走，议事会只有三天重开粮仓。它命获准进入的粮官在肩上系红布，让疲惫的守卫能迅速辨认。办法立刻见效：队伍缩短，混进秤台的人也少了。起初红布只是记号，粮官仍须出示文书，守卫照样核名，每晚还要把布条交回一只普通木盘。
许多年过去，红色爬上印章、门牌、座椅，后来连官员子女的衣领也用它。商贩见红让路，伙计收起私账，旅店把红衣客人换进好房。新守卫没经历过火灾，也不再问文书。一次临时捷径开始真正打开门、改变价格，还决定谁的诉求先被听见；这些后果又反过来让身份差异显得天经地义。
裁缝学徒小辛赶着在典礼前送回粮官外套，为免红布拖到泥里，便把它搭在自己肩上。守卫主动放行，仓吏递来钥匙，排队请愿的人也纷纷退开。小辛先说自己不是官员，随后想到师傅迟交要受罚，便沉默着穿过三间禁入库房，提前送到了衣服。
一册粮账失踪后，他因有人记得“红肩的人”而被怀疑。粮官不承认借出身份，守卫则坚持红色自古就代表权威。档案员找出火灾后的原令，上面只写“为便于辨认，暂用红布”。布本身没有天生力量，几十年的规章、让路、任命与惩罚却让违逆它变得昂贵。即使原句已经摊在桌上，小辛仍承受着被指控的真实代价。

重开以前，议事会试了三道门：一道核文书，一道只认颜色，一道让官员不戴布。相同的人因布周围的规则不同，得到的速度、怀疑和通行权也不同。雨水仍会毁粮，锁门仍能挡住身体，但红色附着的等级会随共同做法改变，并不藏在染料里面。粮仓恢复文书核验，也登记每条红布由谁领用。一些官员抱怨门口变慢，因为检查暴露了他们早已视作寻常的便利。账本最终在另一间官署找到，小辛却少领了一周工钱。回店后，他把红布折进木盘，没有再搭上肩；街外，人们仍在为下一个穿红的人让路。
explanationParagraphs: Social construction describes how categories, identities, institutions, and meanings arise through historical decisions, repeated interaction, classification, and power, then come to appear externally real. Constructed does not mean false or materially harmless, nor easily changed by one person. The question is how something was produced, maintained, and internalised.
explanationParagraphsZh: 社会建构描述类别、身份、制度与意义如何由历史决定、重复互动、分类和权力形成，并逐渐被当作外在现实。被建构不等于虚假或没有物质后果，也不表示可以由个人随意改变；关键是具体追问它怎样产生、维持并被人内化。

articles.title: The Table Before the Guest Spoke
articles.summary: A waiter knows who should sit first without consulting a rulebook until every natural movement is misplaced in another dining room.
articles.summaryZh: 一名侍者不用背规则便知道谁先落座，换到另一间餐厅后，这些自然动作却全都错了位。
storyParagraphs: Yanqing had served in a marquis's house for ten years. From cloth, gait, and number of attendants, he knew who belonged in the principal seat. Before a guest spoke, wine stood at the right hand and the softest chair awaited the highest rank. No complete rulebook described these movements, and he rarely thought about them.

When the household closed, Yanqing joined a cooperative restaurant by the harbour. Sailors, owners, and cooks shared long tables. Whoever arrived first sat first, and dishes travelled from the nearest place. Yanqing still stopped people in worn clothes and saved seats for well-dressed guests. He waited for a 'host' to lift chopsticks while the whole table waited for him to serve.

His colleagues thought him proud; Yanqing thought the harbour lacked manners. During one busy evening, he saw the restaurant owner washing dishes with rolled sleeves while the guest in silk was merely waiting for a boat repair. Judgements that had usually worked in the old house repeatedly misplaced people here.

Yanqing began following his colleagues. He asked about party size and needs rather than guessing from clothing. At staff meals, he made himself take food before the owner. Every movement felt wrong at first. After several months, he could shift between different practices in different dining rooms.

The change did not come smoothly. When a marquis's former steward booked a banquet, Yanqing slipped back into the old rhythm: he held dishes until the steward began, shifted a fisherwoman away from the soft chair, and nearly delayed an entire table. The cooperative owner offered to remove him from service, but Yanqing asked to lose a week's share instead and work every kind of shift. He served dock breakfasts, family meals, and union suppers, writing down each mistaken guess. Colleagues showed him which cues mattered here—who had reserved space, who needed a backrest, who was carrying food—not who looked important. Months later, returning briefly to a noble house, his hands recovered the old sequence before he had consciously named it. Back at the harbour that night, he nearly waited for the owner again, then saw the cook reach first and took food with him. His notebook now held crossed-out guesses beside newer questions, and the soft chair moved toward aching backs rather than silk sleeves.

One quiet night, a richly dressed guest entered alone. Yanqing did not pull out the principal chair. His hand moved halfway toward it, stopped, and rested on the ordinary chair beside him. After a pause, he asked, 'Which table are you joining?'
storyParagraphsZh: 彦青在侯爵家做了十年侍者。门一开，他便能从衣料、步伐和随从人数看出谁该坐主位。客人尚未开口，他已经把酒放在右手边，把最软的椅子留给身份最高的人。这些动作从未写成完整规则，他也几乎不用思考。
侯爵府关闭后，彦青去了港口合伙餐厅。那里船工、老板和厨师共用长桌，先到的人先坐，菜也从最近处传递。彦青仍会拦住穿旧衣的人，把空位留给衣着体面的客人；他还站着等“主人”先动筷，整桌人却都在等他上菜。
同事觉得他傲慢，彦青则认为港口毫无礼数。直到一次忙乱中，他看见餐厅老板卷着袖子洗碗，而穿丝衣的客人只是来修船。他熟悉的判断在旧府里常常有效，到了新地方却不断把人放错位置。
彦青开始跟着同事工作。他练习先问人数与需要，不再从衣服猜座位；吃员工饭时，也强迫自己在老板之前夹菜。起初每个动作都别扭，几个月后，他能在两种宴席间换回不同做法。

改变并不顺利。一名侯爵旧管事预订宴席时，彦青立刻退回旧节奏：等管事动筷才上菜，把渔妇从软椅边请走，还险些让整桌冷掉。合伙人准备撤掉他的服务班次，彦青却请求少分一周收入，换来轮做各种时段。他端过码头早餐、家庭聚餐和工会晚饭，把每次猜错都写下。同事让他看这里真正有用的线索：谁订了座、谁需要靠背、谁正端着食物，而不是谁看起来尊贵。几个月后，他短暂回旧府帮工，双手又在来得及思考前恢复了原有次序。那晚回港，他差点再次等老板动筷，看见厨师已经伸手，才跟着夹菜。本子里，猜错的身份被一道道划去，旁边换成新问题；软椅也开始跟着酸痛的后背移动，不再追随丝绸袖口。
某晚，一位衣着华贵的客人独自进门。彦青的手已经伸向主位，又在半途停住，落到旁边的普通椅背上。他停了一息，没有替对方决定，只问：“您和哪一桌的人同行？”
explanationParagraphs: Habitus is a relatively durable set of dispositions formed through social experience. It shapes perception, expectation, taste, and action, making many practices feel natural without conscious rules. Habitus always operates within a field and with available resources, so a disposition that fits one setting can misfire in another. It is durable but not unchangeable.
explanationParagraphsZh: 惯习是社会经历形成的相对持久倾向，塑造人的感知、期待、品味和行动，使许多做法无需逐条思考便显得自然。它总与具体场域和实际可用资源共同运作，因此在一处合适的倾向可能在另一处错位。惯习持久但并非不可改变。

articles.title: The Empty Bench on a Full Ferry
articles.summary: The ferry is too crowded to turn around, yet the long bench at the bow remains empty.
articles.summaryZh: 渡船已经挤得无人能转身，船头那张长椅却仍然空着。
storyParagraphs: A long bench stood at the bow of the Green Bay ferry. No sign said who could sit there, yet passengers knew it was reserved for guild elders. Even when no elder travelled, ordinary people remained standing. Anyone who moved too close received coughs, stares, or a warning not to ignore custom.

One stormy day, other crossings closed and the cabin filled. A stonemason named Aman, whose leg was bandaged, sat on the bench. The ticket collector did not stop him, but passengers immediately began talking. Some complained that young people had become selfish, while others refused to pass his baggage along.

At the next stop, a guild elder boarded. Aman prepared to rise, but the elder saw his injury and sat on a wooden box. Several passengers still urged Aman to move, as though the elder's own choice could not cancel the unwritten rule.

The elder asked who had established the bench. No one could answer. They only remembered that a passenger had once been condemned by the whole ferry for refusing to move. The elder sat beside Aman and placed his luggage between them. No one coughed during the remaining crossing.

At the return landing, the ticket collector proposed a sign giving priority to injured passengers, carers, and anyone unable to stand safely. Several regulars objected, not because an elder needed the seat that day, but because changing the rule would expose their earlier scolding as a choice. One passenger who privately agreed stayed silent until another accused him of failing to defend tradition. He then joined the complaint. The pressure reached not only the person who sat down, but also anyone who declined to punish him.

The elder refused to issue a new privilege in his own name. He paid for an open meeting and accepted that the ferry would depart late. Passengers argued over safety, age, disability, and whether any group should own the whole bench. One regular demanded punishment for anyone who failed to challenge an improper sitter; a woman replied that this threat had kept her from helping an injured neighbour. They finally adopted a visible priority rule, a review date, and a request that the collector intervene before the crowd did. The ferry lost one busy crossing, and the guild complained about surrendered status, but the next storm left no injured passenger standing.

There was still no new sign the next day. A man carrying a child sat first, and a nearby passenger moved his bag closer to his feet. The collector unfolded the agreed rule at the ticket table and marked the date when everyone would review it after one month.
storyParagraphsZh: 青湾渡船的船头有一张长椅。没有告示规定谁能坐，乘客却都知道那是留给行会长老的。即使长老不在，普通人也宁愿站着。有人靠得太近，旁边乘客便会咳嗽、盯视，或提醒他“别不懂规矩”。
一天风雨封了其他渡口，船舱挤得满满当当。腿上缠着绷带的石匠阿满坐上长椅。售票员没有阻止，周围乘客却立刻议论。有人说年轻人越来越自私，还有人故意不替他传递行李。
下一站，行会长老上船。阿满正要起身，长老看见他的伤，坐到了木箱上。几名乘客仍催阿满让座，仿佛长老本人的选择也不能取消这条没有写下的规矩。
长老问是谁定下这张椅子。没人答得出，只记得曾有人因不让座被全船责骂。长老随后坐到阿满身边，把自己的行李放在两人中间。余下航程里，再没有人咳嗽。
返航靠岸时，售票员建议立一块牌，让伤者、照护者和无法安全站立的人优先。几名常客反对，并非当天真有长老需要座位，而是改规矩会暴露他们过去的斥责原本是一种选择。有个乘客私下赞成，却被指责“不维护传统”后立刻加入抱怨。压力不只落在坐下的人身上，也落在每个拒绝惩罚他的人身上。
长老没有用自己的名义再设一种特权，而是出钱召开公开讨论，接受渡船晚发一班。众人争论安全、年龄、身体需要和是否该由任何群体独占整椅。有人要求惩罚每个不斥责“乱坐者”的乘客，一名妇人却说，正是这种威胁让她不敢帮助受伤邻居。最后大家订下可见的优先规则、复查日期，并要求售票员先于人群介入。渡船损失了一趟繁忙航次，行会也埋怨地位受损；下一场风雨里，却再没有伤者站着。
第二天，长椅上仍没有新告示。一个抱着孩子的男人先坐了下来，旁边的人看了一眼，替他把行李推到脚边。售票员在桌上展开共同订下的规则，又圈出一个月后所有人约定复查它的日期。
explanationParagraphs: Norm enforcement maintains shared expectations through approval, reminders, shame, exclusion, punishment, or sanctions against those who fail to intervene, often without written law. Enforcement may be distributed among peers or organised formally. A persistent norm is not necessarily fair; power, visibility, and unequal ability to sanction shape who is constrained.
explanationParagraphsZh: 规范执行通过赞许、提醒、羞辱、排斥、惩罚或制裁不干预者来维持共同期待，往往无需成文法律。执行可以分散在同伴之间，也可能由正式机构承担。规范持续存在不代表它公平；权力、可见性和制裁能力会决定谁更容易被约束。

articles.title: The Dam That Broke Before Dawn
articles.summary: Three callers report that the north dam has failed, but a reporter finds they are repeating one sentence from an inn.
articles.summaryZh: 三名来电者都说北坝已经决口，记者却发现他们只是重复旅店里的一句话。
storyParagraphs: At three in the morning, reporter Su Yan received a call saying the north dam had broken. Within ten minutes, two more people reported the same thing. The morning edition was closing, and her editor urged her to write 'according to multiple witnesses' before another paper published first.

Su Yan asked each caller where they had seen the flood. The first had heard it from an innkeeper. The second had heard it from the first caller's brother. The third had only seen people running beside the river. Three reports sounded independent but returned to one sentence spoken at the inn.

The duty water officer did not answer, so Su Yan rode to a hill overlooking the north dam. The wall still stood. One spillway gate was open. People running by the river were moving tools from low ground, not escaping a breach.

The paper reported: no breach observed at the north dam; one gate opened overnight; reason awaiting confirmation from the water office. The cautious line cost Su Yan the first edition's largest headline, and a rival paper printed the collapse as fact. Families began moving uphill anyway. She returned to the river, photographed fixed points on the intact wall, noted the time, and asked two downstream villages what water had actually reached them rather than whether they had heard a breach.

After dawn, officials said rising upstream water had triggered a planned release. Su Yan requested the operating log instead of copying the statement. The recorded gate time matched her photographs and downstream observations, but one warning had reached the lower village late. Her update corrected the false collapse without turning the official explanation into a blanket declaration that nothing had gone wrong. It separated wall condition, gate action, flood level, warning time, and remaining uncertainty.

Before the next edition, Su Yan called the three informants and explained what had changed. One was angry that his name would no longer count as a witness; another admitted he had repeated the warning to be safe. She preserved both reactions, added a correction box beside the rival claim, and wrote a checklist for location, access, independence, time, and competing explanations.

Her editor crushed the prepared 'multiple witnesses' headline. Su Yan kept the three call notes and drew a line from each back to the same inn. Beside the lines she attached the hill photograph, gate log, downstream measurements, and the late-warning time, each labelled with what it could and could not establish. The empty headline space remained visible through the next print run.
storyParagraphsZh: 凌晨三点，记者苏雁接到电话，说北坝已经决口。十分钟内，又有两个人打来同样消息。早报截稿将近，编辑催她先写“据多名目击者称”，免得被别家抢先。
苏雁分别问三人从哪里看见洪水。第一人听旅店老板说，第二人从第一人的弟弟那里得知，第三人只看见河边有人奔跑。三条消息听起来独立，最后却都指向旅店里同一句传闻。
她打给值班水利员，无人接听，便骑车到能望见北坝的高坡。坝身仍在，一道泄洪闸却打开了。河边奔跑的人正在转移低处工具，并非逃离决口。
早报最终写道：北坝未发现决口，夜间开启一处闸门，开闸原因尚待水利部门确认。谨慎表述让苏雁失去初版最大标题，另一家报纸却把决堤当事实印出，许多家庭仍开始往高处搬。她再次回河边，拍下坝墙固定位置并标注时间，又问下游两村实际到了多少水，而不是问他们是否听说决口。
天亮后，水利部门称上游涨水触发了预定泄洪。苏雁没有照抄，而是索要值班日志。开闸时间与她的照片和下游观察相符，但一条警报确实晚到低处村庄。更新稿纠正“决堤”，却没有把官方说明写成“一切无事”，而是分别交代坝体、闸门、水位、警报时间与仍待确认之处。
下一版截稿前，苏雁逐一回电，明确告诉三名报料者哪些内容已经改变。有人恼怒自己不再被称为目击者，也有人承认只是怕出事才把警告传开。她把两种反应都留在笔记里，在错误报道旁加上更正框，又写下地点、接触能力、独立性、时间和替代解释五项检查。
编辑把原先拟好的“多名目击者”标题揉成一团。苏雁没有丢掉三份通话记录，而是在每份上画线，连回同一家旅店。线旁又贴着高坡照片、闸门日志、下游水位与迟到警报时间，每项都注明能证明什么、不能证明什么。下一轮正式印刷时，撤掉标题留下的空位仍然清楚可见。
explanationParagraphs: Journalistic verification tests claims by tracing original sources, assessing their access and interests, observing directly, seeking independent corroboration, checking context, and comparing alternatives. Multiple retellings do not necessarily provide independent evidence. Responsible reporting separates known, inferred, disputed, and unknown claims and updates as evidence changes.
explanationParagraphsZh: 新闻核实通过追踪原始来源、检查来源能力与利益、直接观察、独立佐证、语境和替代解释来检验主张。多名转述者不一定是多个独立来源。负责任报道会明确区分已知、推断、争议与未知，并在证据变化时公开更正和持续更新。

articles.title: A Noticeboard with Room for Three Things
articles.titleZh: 只能容下三件事的公告板
articles.summary: The newspaper can pin only three pages outside each day, and the town begins treating those three things as the whole city.
articles.summaryZh: 报馆每天只能把三张纸贴到门外，镇民渐渐把那三件事当成了整座城。
storyParagraphs: The River Mouth newspaper had room for three front pages on its outdoor board. Each day, the editor chose among a mayoral speech, a bridge opening, a visiting theatre, salty well water, and staff shortages at the clinic. The speech arrived ready to print, the bridge offered a strong photograph, and the theatre sold papers. Those three filled the board.

For two weeks, the water problem appeared only in a corner inside. When the council asked residents what concerned them, most first named the bridge and theatre. This did not make them agree about the bridge or share one opinion of the performers. Those were simply the names appearing at the door each day.

A young reporter named A-He stacked readers' letters by subject on the editor's desk. The pile about well water had become the tallest, yet the paper still judged it 'not a major story'. Only after a teahouse closed because of salty water did the issue reach the front page. The next day, the council received a sudden increase in related questions.

The mayor accused the paper of manufacturing panic, while theatre owners demanded their poster return to the board. The editor tried one week of reader voting. Bridge photographs still won early because they were familiar, while clinic workers on night shifts submitted few ballots. A-He mapped letters, council questions, searches at the reading room, and events such as the closed teahouse. Each signal had a different bias, but together they showed that choosing what deserved scarce attention could not be outsourced to the easiest material or the loudest voters.

One page had not created the salty water, and the newspaper could not command an opinion. Readers who ranked water first still disagreed over pipes, wells, and municipal spending. But scarce space repeatedly suggested which matters deserved to be thought about, questioned, and discussed first. The editor sacrificed a profitable theatre advertisement, published a visible list of stories left out, and reserved one rotating place for issues that had stayed in corners despite accumulating evidence.

A month later the board carried clinic staffing, well water, and the bridge budget. Residents argued fiercely over remedies, proving that prominence had not produced agreement. The editor compared letters before and after coverage and noticed that public questions also redirected reporters toward new documents. Attention moved both ways: publication changed conversation, while events and readers pushed back on publication choices.
At dusk, A-He removed the expired theatre poster and pinned the stack of water letters beside the board. She left one empty pin beneath the published list of omitted stories.
storyParagraphsZh: 河口报馆门外的公告板只能容下三张头条。编辑每天都要选择：市长演说、桥梁开工、戏班来访、井水变咸、诊所缺人。演说有现成稿件，开工有漂亮照片，戏班又能卖报，三张纸很快占满。
井水问题连续两周只出现在内页一角。镇议会询问居民最关心什么时，多数人先说桥和戏班。没人因此赞成同一种桥，也没人对戏班评价相同；只是这些名字每天都在门口出现。
年轻记者阿禾把读者来信按主题叠在编辑桌上。关于井水的信已经最高，报馆却仍觉得它“不像大事”。直到一家茶馆因咸水停业，编辑才把井水放上头条。第二天，镇议会收到的相关提问突然增加。
市长指责报馆制造恐慌，戏班老板也要求海报回到公告板。编辑试行一周读者投票，熟悉的桥梁照片仍最早得票，值夜班的诊所人员却很少有空投票。阿禾把来信、议会提问、阅览室检索和茶馆停业等事件分别画成线。每种信号都有偏差，但它们共同提醒编辑：稀缺注意不能外包给最容易取得的材料或声音最大的人。
报馆没有凭一张纸制造咸水，也不能命令居民持何种观点；即使都把水列在首位，人们仍会争论修管道、换井还是增加公共支出。但有限的位置会反复提示哪些事情值得先想、先问、先讨论。编辑放弃一份赚钱的戏班广告，公开每天落选题目，并留出一个轮换位置，给那些证据不断累积却长期挤在角落的报道。
一个月后，公告板同时放着诊所人手、井水和桥梁预算。居民为解决办法争得厉害，足以证明显眼并没有制造一致观点。编辑比较报道前后的来信，又发现公众提问会把记者推向新的文件。注意力并非只从报馆流向街道：刊登改变讨论，现实事件与读者也会反过来改变报馆选择。
傍晚，阿禾撤下过期的戏班海报，把那叠关于井水的来信钉在公告板旁边；每日落选清单下面，还留着一枚空钉。
explanationParagraphs: Agenda-setting describes how the frequency, position, and prominence of media coverage influence which issues people consider important. It more directly affects issue salience than agreement with a particular view. Media agendas also interact with real events, politics, interpersonal discussion, platforms, and the public's existing interests.
explanationParagraphsZh: 议程设置描述媒体对议题的频率、位置和突出程度如何影响公众认为哪些问题重要。它通常更直接改变议题显著性，而非让人接受特定观点。媒体议程还会与现实事件、政治、人际讨论、不同传播平台和公众既有兴趣相互作用。

articles.title: Three Voices from One Mouth
articles.titleZh: 来自同一张嘴的三个声音
articles.summary: A reporter finds three people who confirm a grain ship has sunk, then discovers they all heard the same story.
articles.summaryZh: 记者找到三个人证明粮船沉没，追问下去却发现他们都听过同一个故事。
storyParagraphs: A rumour spread through the harbour: the month's grain ship had sunk at sea and the city would soon run short. Reporter Chi Qing found three sources. A grain merchant said the vessel was gone. A dockworker said the same. An innkeeper claimed to have heard a crewman admit it. Her editor considered three agreeing sources enough to print.

Chi Qing asked the merchant where he had learned the news; he pointed to the dockworker's brother. The dockworker had heard talk at the inn. The innkeeper's 'crewman' was actually a porter employed by the grain merchant. The three voices formed a circle leading back to the merchant's first statement.

She did not therefore assume the ship was safe. The departure list confirmed it was two days late. Customs reported that it had sheltered at a neighbouring port. Warehouse stocks and market prices showed no current shortage. Each line answered a different part: where the ship was, how much grain remained, and whether prices were changing.

The merchant offered Chi Qing an unsigned message said to come from the captain. Its wording matched the inn rumour, adding apparent confirmation without a new path to the ship. She asked customs for the time-stamped harbour entry, sent a colleague to count sacks with a warehouse worker, and compared retail prices collected independently from four markets. Customs could locate the vessel; the count could estimate supply; prices could show current pressure. None answered every part, and each could fail differently.

The report stated: grain vessel delayed by sheltering; no evidence of sinking; some stores may reduce sales in six days if delay continues. When one warehouse disputed her count, she published its method and range rather than forcing agreement. The merchant, dock, inn, and captain message were identified as one chain of retelling, while the manifest, customs record, physical count, and price sample remained separate lines with stated limits.

Before publication, she tried to break each line herself. A second customs clerk verified the register, a different worker repeated the sack count, and the four price observations were dated and kept separate. One market moved against the others because a local stall had closed; that disagreement narrowed the claim instead of being discarded. Her editor accepted the delay and lost the afternoon sales advantage.

Before final layout, Chi Qing replaced the three separate names with one connected line and added the manifest, customs record, warehouse count, and dated price sample beside it. The unsupported captain's note still remained safely sealed in a separate sleeve.
storyParagraphsZh: 港口突然传出消息：本月粮船在外海沉没，城里很快会缺粮。记者迟青找到三名消息来源。米商说船没了，码头工也这样说，客栈老板还听见船员亲口承认。编辑认为三方一致，准备刊出。
迟青问米商从哪里得知，他指向码头工的兄长；码头工听的是客栈传闻；客栈老板所说的“船员”，其实是米商雇来运货的人。三个声音绕了一圈，都回到米商最先说出的那句话。
她没有因此认定粮船平安。迟青去查出港清单，发现船确实晚了两日；又向海关核对，得知它在邻港避风；最后比较仓库实存与市场价格，尚未看到短缺。不同线索分别回答船在哪里、粮有多少和价格是否变化。
米商又交给迟青一张据称来自船长的无署名便条，措辞却与客栈传闻相同，只让旧说法看起来多了一层，并未增加通向船只的新路径。她向海关索取带时间的入港记录，派同事和仓工一起点数粮袋，又独立收集四处市场价格。海关回答船在哪，盘点估算粮有多少，价格显示眼前压力；没有一项包办全部，而且各有不同的出错方式。
报道写成：粮船因避风延迟，未发现沉没证据；若继续晚到，部分仓库可能在六日后减量。一家仓库质疑点数时，她公开方法与范围，没有强求整齐一致。米商、码头、客栈和船长便条被注明属于同一传闻链；清单、海关、实物盘点和价格样本则作为路径不同、边界明确的线索。
刊出以前，她主动尝试推翻每条线索：请第二名海关书记复核登记，让另一名仓工重做盘点，把四处价格按日期分别保存。其中一个市场因摊位停业而逆向变动；她没有删掉分歧，而是据此缩小价格结论。编辑接受延迟，也失去了午后抢先卖报的优势。
排版前，迟青把原来并排的三个姓名画成一条相连的线，又在旁边添上清单、海关、仓库盘点与带日期的价格样本。无法独立追溯的船长便条，被留在另一只纸套里。
explanationParagraphs: Source triangulation uses sources, data, or methods with genuinely different access paths, interests, and failure modes to evaluate a claim. Quantity is not independence; many retellings can share one origin. Converging evidence may increase confidence, while disagreement can reveal error or show that sources answer different parts of a claim.
explanationParagraphsZh: 来源三角验证使用接触路径、利益和失败方式不同的来源、资料或方法来评价同一主张。数量不等于独立性；多名转述者可能共享一个原始来源。不同证据的汇合可增强信心，分歧则可能暴露错误或说明它们回答的是不同部分。

articles.fieldTitleZh: 图书馆、信息与档案研究
articles.title: The Letter That Arrived Without a Past
articles.summary: A letter said to rewrite a dynasty's history reaches the archive without an envelope, recipient, or custody record.
articles.summaryZh: 一封据称能改写王朝史的旧信来到档案馆，却没有信封、收件人或保管记录。
storyParagraphs: A collector brought an old letter said to be written by the last queen, proving that she had ordered an end to a war. The paper was old and the hand resembled court writing. Buying it could make the archive famous, but a young archivist first asked where it had come from.

The collector knew only that it had been purchased in a country chest. There was no envelope, the ending was missing, and the chest had changed owners several times. Watermarks, folds, and an old number suggested that the letter might once have belonged with theatre manuscripts rather than court papers.

They followed sale records to the chest's previous owner. The elderly man remembered that his grandfather copied historical plays and made props in old-fashioned handwriting. The paper did belong to the period, but nothing showed that it had entered the palace or reached a military commander.

The collector cut his price in half and warned that another museum would announce the royal discovery that week. The director wanted the crowded exhibition hall and donor attention such a claim could bring. The young archivist asked for one day and laid out every relationship: the chest sale, theatre inventory number, grandfather's copying work, paper watermark, missing ending, and the years no owner could account for. Old material and plausible handwriting established age and resemblance, not palace custody or the action described in the text.

The archive still accepted the letter, losing the chance to advertise it as the queen's command. It preserved the collector's correspondence and acquisition decision with the item, but catalogued the letter among the theatre manager's papers rather than separating it into a royal collection. Its entry recorded the paper date, use context, related manuscripts, custody gap, and uncertain author. It might be a prop or a copy of an earlier text; the surviving relationships supported its theatre history more strongly than its royal claim.

Months later, a scholar requested the supposed order. The archivist supplied the whole file and watched him revise his question from 'Why did the queen stop the war?' to 'How did a theatre reuse royal language?' The letter had lost a sensational label but gained a claim the surrounding records could support. Its uncertain passage through the missing years remained visible in the catalogue rather than repaired by a confident story.

When storing it, the archivist did not number the letter alone. She placed the chest records, acquisition correspondence, and theatre manuscripts in the same archival box. The rejected royal caption stayed in the acquisition file as part of the archive's own decision history.
storyParagraphsZh: 收藏商带来一封旧信，说它出自末代王后，证明她曾命人停止战争。纸张古老，字迹也像宫廷手书。馆长若买下它，档案馆会因此闻名；年轻档案员却先问信从哪里来。
收藏商只知道它购自一只乡间木箱。信没有信封，末尾缺页，木箱也已转手多次。档案员查看水印、折痕和旧编号，发现它原本可能与一叠剧院文稿放在一起，而不是宫廷公文。
他们沿买卖记录找到木箱上一任主人。老人记得祖父在剧团抄写历史戏，常用旧式字迹制作道具。信的纸确实属于那个年代，却没有证据表明曾进入宫廷或送到任何将领手中。
收藏商把价格降到一半，还警告另一家博物馆本周就会公布“王后发现”。馆长渴望那条消息带来的观众与捐赠。年轻档案员只争取一天，把关系逐项铺开：木箱买卖、剧团编号、老人祖父的抄写工作、纸张水印、缺失结尾，以及无人能说明的保管年份。旧纸与相似字迹只能支持年代和外观，不能建立宫廷保管，也不能证明信中命令真正执行。
档案馆仍然收下这封信，却放弃以王后命令宣传。它把收藏商来信和收购决定与实物一同保留，并按剧院经理的文件群归档，没有单独抽成“王室藏品”。目录写明纸张年代、使用语境、相关剧本、保管空缺和不明作者。信可能是道具，也可能抄自更早文本；现有文件关系对剧院历史的支持远强于王室主张。
几个月后，一名学者来查那份“王后命令”。档案员交出整组文件，看着他把问题从“王后为何停战”改成“剧团怎样借用王室语言”。这封信失去了轰动标签，却得到周边记录能支持的用途；那些无人能说明的流转年份仍留在目录里，没有被一个自信故事补平。
入库时，档案员没有只给信编号。她把木箱转手记录、收购来信和剧团文稿一起装进了同一只档案盒。那张被否决的王室说明牌也留在收购卷里，成为档案馆自身决定过程的一部分。
explanationParagraphs: Provenance concerns who created and used a record, in what activity, and how custody or control changed. Preserving those relationships helps evaluate authenticity and meaning but does not prove that a record's statements are true. Gaps in custody, copying, multiple creators, and disturbed original order should be documented explicitly.
explanationParagraphsZh: 来源原则关注记录由谁、在什么活动中创建和使用，以及保管与控制如何变化。保存这些关系有助于判断真实性与意义，但不能自动证明记录内容为真。保管空缺、复制、多重创建者和原始秩序受损等具体情况都应得到明确记录。

articles.fieldTitleZh: 图书馆、信息与档案研究
articles.title: The Warehouse That Had Everything
articles.summary: A relief warehouse owns everything the city might need but cannot find the boxes of children's winter clothes when snow arrives.
articles.summaryZh: 救济仓库什么都有，暴雪来临时却找不到哪只箱子里装着儿童冬衣。
storyParagraphs: The North City relief warehouse was packed with donations from floor to rafters. Its manager proudly said that whatever the city needed could be found there. Most boxes were marked only 'clothing', 'supplies', or with the donor's name.

Before a blizzard closed the roads, a shelter urgently requested children's winter clothes. The manager knew many had arrived the previous year, but workers had to open boxes one by one. Some marked 'clothing' contained adult summer wear. Others had moved while the list still pointed to an old shelf. The first delivery cart left before the winter clothes were found.

The manager first blamed the workers and ordered larger labels. A week later, two boxes carrying the same new label proved to contain different sizes, while a perfectly described medicine box could not be released because its donor restriction had expired. Description alone was not enough. The records also needed locations, relationships between sets, access terms, formats, inspection dates, and responsibility for updates. Every choice of field made some searches easier and left other distinctions invisible.

After the snow, the manager cancelled an order for more shelving and used the money to catalogue what was already there. Workers agreed on terms, photographed unclear contents, linked coats to their detachable liners, recorded who could use restricted donations, and made a move scan update location instead of physically fixing boxes in one permanent order. They also marked uncertain entries and assigned monthly checks, because a clean catalogue that stopped changing would soon become another lost shelf list.

When the shelter later requested twenty infant blankets, a worker filtered the catalogue and followed two shelf numbers to the right boxes. The records did not warm anyone, but they allowed the actual blankets to arrive on time.

Three months later a software change dropped the donor-restriction field during migration. A worker caught it because the catalogue count no longer matched the monthly rights report. The manager stopped dispatch for an afternoon, restored the field from backups, and documented the transformation. Fast search depended not only on initial description but on maintenance, permissions, preservation, and honest correction when records drifted.

After dispatch, the manager reduced the quantity in the catalogue, recorded the transaction, and reserved the empty shelf for the next delivery. He clipped the missed winter-clothing request to the catalogue manual so every new worker and future software keeper would know why each field, update, uncertainty mark, rights note, and preservation check mattered greatly during a real emergency before the next blizzard closed the road.
storyParagraphsZh: 北城救济仓库堆满捐赠物。箱子从地面码到屋梁，管理员自豪地说城里需要什么，这里都有。多数箱面只写着“衣物”“用品”或捐赠人的姓名。
暴雪封路前，避难所急需儿童冬衣。管理员知道去年收过很多，却只能一箱箱拆开。有些“衣物”全是成人夏装，有些箱子换过位置，清单仍指向旧货架。等找到冬衣时，第一辆送货车已经离开。
管理员起初责怪伙计，命人换上更大的标签。一周后，两只同样写着“冬衣”的箱子装着不同尺码；另一只药箱描述得很清楚，却因捐赠限制已经过期而不能发放。仅有名称还不够，记录还需要位置、套件关系、使用权限、格式、检查日期和更新责任。每选一个字段，就会让某些查找更容易，也让另一些差异继续看不见。
雪停后，管理员取消新购货架，把钱用于整理现有物资。伙计统一词语，为难辨内容拍照，把外套与可拆内衬关联起来，记录限制物资由谁使用；箱子移动时扫描更新位置，而不是强迫实物永远维持一个顺序。他们还标出不确定条目，安排每月复查，因为一份不再变化的漂亮目录，很快又会变成旧货架清单。
下一次避难所需要二十条婴儿毯，伙计先在目录里筛出可用物，再沿货架号找到两个箱子。记录没有替他们保暖，却让真正的毯子及时抵达。
三个月后，软件迁移意外丢掉了“捐赠限制”字段。伙计发现目录数量与每月权利报告对不上，管理员便暂停半天发货，从备份恢复字段，并记录转换过程。快速检索不只靠最初描述，也靠维护、权限、保存，以及记录漂移时如实纠错。
出库后，管理员在目录里改掉数量，记下这次流转，又把空出的货架位置留给下一批物资。他把那张错过送货车的冬衣申请夹进目录手册，让新伙计知道每个字段、更新、不确定标记、权利说明和保存检查为何存在，也记得下一场暴雪封路以前必须复核。
explanationParagraphs: Metadata is structured information used to describe, identify, locate, relate, retrieve, preserve, and manage resources. It can record content, location, format, rights, relationships, and maintenance status. Metadata does not replace the resource and is not neutral: fields, omissions, errors, and updating practices shape what people can find and understand.
explanationParagraphsZh: 元数据是描述、识别、定位、关联、检索、保存和管理资源的结构化信息。它可以记录内容、位置、格式、权利、关系与维护状态。元数据不能替代资源，也并非天然中立；字段设计、遗漏、错误和更新方式会影响人们能发现和理解什么。

articles.fieldTitleZh: 图书馆、信息与档案研究
articles.title: The People Missing from Moving Day
articles.summary: A memorial names every official who led the old city's relocation but not the people who actually carried families across the river.
articles.summaryZh: 纪念册列出了所有带领旧城迁移的官员，却没有写下是谁真正把人送过了河。
storyParagraphs: The new city prepared to commemorate a relocation a century earlier. The official register named the officers who signed orders, merchants who financed the move, and male heads of households. Exhibition designers planned portraits from that list. The people who handled boats, divided food, and watched children had no names in it.

Researcher Anhe found writing on the back of an old ferry ticket: 'Lady Liu made three more crossings and took no payment at night.' No formal report mentioned her. The tax roll listed only her husband, although he had died a year before the relocation.

Anhe kept searching. Flour accounts recorded repeated deliveries to 'the women by the river'. A family letter mentioned someone in a red scarf guiding boats at night. Several elders had heard of Lady Liu from grandparents, but could not say whether she acted alone or whether the red scarf belonged to someone else.

The exhibition director wanted one named heroine for the poster and offered Anhe another week if she would complete the portrait. Anhe instead traced where absence had entered: officials had recorded household heads, clerks selected orders for permanent storage, flood damage removed ferry logs, later cataloguers described the move through government offices, and the first exhibition draft repeated those choices. The empty place had not appeared at one moment and could not be repaired by inventing one complete life.

Anhe met descendants of river workers before using the family letter and recordings. Some wanted Lady Liu named; others feared one name would swallow the group again. The exhibition sacrificed its heroic poster and added a wall for 'People Not Entered in the Register', displaying the ticket, flour account, letter, recording conditions, and disagreements in oral memory. Labels separated supported links, plausible readings, and what remained unknown, while visitors could contribute copies without surrendering originals.

At the preview, one official demanded that the empty place be filled or removed. Anhe instead placed a listening bench before it and printed the archive's collection policy beside the wall, showing whose papers it had historically sought. The museum funded new community copying days, but she refused to promise that every missing name would return. Recovery required access, consent, preservation, and time, and some absences would remain.

Before the public opening, she deliberately left a clearly visible space among the officials' portraits and placed the ticket carrying Lady Liu's name at its centre. Beneath it lay pencils and evidence cards; the first visitor contributed a copied boat roster but left its disputed date visibly uncured.
storyParagraphsZh: 新城准备纪念百年前的大迁移。官方名册记录了签署命令的官员、出资商人和各户男性户主，展览设计者便照着名单安排画像。负责运船、分食物和照看孩子的人，在册中没有名字。
研究员安禾在一张旧船票背面发现几行小字：“柳娘再送三船，夜里不收钱。”她查遍正式报告，没有柳娘。税册里只记着她丈夫，丈夫却在迁城前一年已经去世。
安禾继续寻找。面粉账显示同一笔粮连续送到“河边妇人处”，一封家信提到有人用红围巾在夜里引船。几位老人听祖辈说过柳娘，却记不清她是否独自负责，也不知道红围巾是不是另一个人。
展览主任想要一位有姓名的女英雄做海报，答应只要安禾补全画像就多给一周。安禾却追查缺席在哪些环节进入：官员只记户主，书记选择命令永久保存，洪水毁掉渡船日志，后来编目者又从官署角度描述迁移，第一版展览继续沿用这些选择。空处并非一次造成，也不能靠虚构一段完整人生修好。
使用家信和录音前，安禾与河工后代见面。有人希望写出柳娘，有人担心一个名字再次吞没整个群体。展览放弃英雄海报，增加一面“尚未进入名册的人”，放上船票、面粉账、家信、口述采集条件和记忆分歧。标签分开可支持联系、可能解释与未知；访客可以贡献副本，不必交出家中原件。
预展时，一名官员要求把空处填上或撤掉。安禾只在前面放一张听录音的长凳，又把档案馆历年收集政策印在墙边，让人看见它过去主动寻找过谁的文件。馆方出资举办社区复制日，她却拒绝保证每个名字都能回来。补寻需要准入、同意、保存与时间，有些缺席仍会留下。
开幕前，她在官员画像之间留出一块空处，把那张写有柳娘名字的船票放在中央。下方只摆铅笔与证据卡；第一名访客带来一份船工名册副本，安禾收下它，却没有抹平上面仍有争议的日期。
explanationParagraphs: Archival silence is meaningful absence produced during recording, selection, preservation, description, access, or later narration. Power, resources, convention, damage, or accident may create silence; missing records do not prove missing events. Researchers can seek alternative traces and state their limits, but should not replace absence with invented certainty.
explanationParagraphsZh: 档案沉默是记录、选择、保存、描述、开放和后续叙述中具有意义的缺席。沉默可能由权力、资源、惯例、毁损或偶然形成；没有记录并不证明没有发生。研究者可寻找替代痕迹并说明限制，但不应以想象补成未经证实的完整故事。

articles.title: The Coin That Had to Appear Twice
articles.summary: After a shop borrows one hundred coins, its cash box looks rich enough for the owner to mistake debt for profit.
articles.summaryZh: 商铺借来一百枚钱后，钱箱突然丰厚，老板差点把债务当成了利润。
storyParagraphs: A cloth shop borrowed one hundred coins from a bank to buy winter stock. Seeing the full cash box, the owner declared that the month had been profitable and prepared to send some money home. The new bookkeeper, Su Qi, wrote at the same time on another page: 'One hundred coins to be repaid.'

The owner objected that recording one sum twice merely made business difficult. Su Qi asked him to calculate the books with the cash entry alone. They showed increased wealth, while the repayment three months later appeared from nowhere, with no record of when the obligation entered the shop.

Su Qi drew the accounting equation above the ledger: what the shop controlled had to be traced against what it owed and what belonged to the owner. Borrowing raised cash and debt by the same hundred; it created no revenue. Paying twenty for cloth changed cash into inventory rather than creating an immediate loss. The owner tested each entry by asking which accounts changed and whether the equation still held, not by copying a coin mechanically onto two pages.

A customer then paid thirty coins for cloth that had cost eighteen. Cash and sales revenue rose by thirty; inventory fell and the cost of goods sold rose by eighteen. Two linked entries separated the customer's payment from the resources consumed to earn it, leaving twelve before other expenses. When the owner tried to hide a repair by crediting cash and debiting a vague expense, the books still balanced. Su Qi produced the missing receipt and showed why equality could catch omission or arithmetic mismatch but could not certify truth, authority, classification, or value.

At month's end, the two sides balanced. The owner still could not treat balance as proof that every transaction was real, since a fictional transaction could also be entered equally. They compared the books with receipts, cloth, and the cash box.

Before closing the month, Su Qi gave the owner four source documents and four proposed entries. He found one amount reversed, one sale recorded without the related inventory cost, and one balanced repair lacking authorisation. Correcting them changed profit without changing the physical cash already present. The shop paid for an independent stock count, sacrificing a trading morning to connect the equal columns back to cloth, obligations, and approved events.

On repayment day, Su Qi removed one hundred coins from cash and the same amount from the debt page. The owner checked the bank receipt, debt agreement, and ledger before signing. Only after appearing in both accounts—and matching the dated outside evidence—did the obligation and money leave the shop together.
storyParagraphsZh: 绸布店为进冬货向银庄借了一百枚钱。老板看见钱箱装满，便说这个月赚得不错，准备先分一部分给家里。新账房苏祁却在账本另一页同时写下“一百枚应归还”。
老板不高兴，认为同一笔钱写两次像是在故意把生意弄复杂。苏祁让他把借款只记进钱箱试算。账上显示财富增加，三个月后的还款却像凭空出现，根本找不到它从哪一天进入商铺。
苏祁在账本上方写下会计等式：商铺控制的东西，必须与欠别人的和归老板的部分一同追踪。借款让现金与债务各增一百，不产生收入；用二十枚进布，只是把现金换成存货，也不会立刻形成全部损失。老板开始逐笔追问哪些账户改变、等式是否仍成立，而不是机械地把硬币抄两遍。
随后顾客用三十枚买走成本十八枚的布。现金与销售收入增加三十；存货减少十八，销售成本增加十八。两组相连分录把收款与为赚取它而耗用的资源分开，其他费用前留下十二。老板又试图把一项虚构维修同时记入现金和杂费，账照样平衡。苏祁拿出缺失凭证，说明相等能暴露遗漏或算错，却不能保证交易真实、获准、分类和估值正确。
月底，左右记录相等。老板仍不能只凭平衡断定所有交易真实，因为一笔虚构交易也能写得相等。他们又把账本同收据、布匹和钱箱逐项核对。
月底前，苏祁给老板四张凭证和四组候选分录。他找出一笔方向写反、一笔销售漏记相关存货成本，还有一项左右相等却未经批准的维修。纠正它们改变了利润，却没有改变已在箱中的现金。店铺停业一个上午，请人独立盘货，把相等栏位重新连回布匹、义务和获准发生的事情。
还款那天，苏祁从钱箱减去一百枚，也从欠款页划去同样数目。老板先核对银庄收据、借款契约与账本才签字。那笔钱进入两个账户并与带日期的外部凭证相合后，现金和偿债义务才一起离开商铺。
explanationParagraphs: Double-entry bookkeeping records each transaction as equal debits and credits across at least two accounts, maintaining the accounting equation and showing simultaneous changes in assets, liabilities, equity, revenue, and expenses. Balance helps reveal inconsistency but does not prove that a transaction was real, authorised, or classified correctly; evidence and controls remain necessary.
explanationParagraphsZh: 复式记账让每项交易以相等的借方与贷方进入至少两个账户，维持会计等式，并显示资产、负债、权益、收入和费用怎样同时变化。分录平衡有助于发现不一致，却不能证明交易真实、获授权或分类正确，仍需凭证、盘点与控制。

articles.title: Spring Paying for Winter
articles.summary: An inn burns a full store of coal in winter but receives the bill in spring, making both seasons look unlike themselves.
articles.summaryZh: 旅店冬天烧完了整仓煤，账单却到春天才来，两个季节因此看起来都不像自己。
storyParagraphs: During a severe winter, a mountain inn bought an entire store of coal on credit, agreeing to pay after the thaw. Every room stayed full and cash accumulated. The owner recorded only money received and paid, so winter looked exceptionally profitable. He prepared to spend the 'surplus' on a larger wine cellar.

Guest numbers fell in spring, just as the coal merchant arrived with the full bill. After payment, the spring account showed a large loss. The owner blamed weak spring business, forgetting that the money purchased fires already consumed during winter.

The bookkeeper refused to treat the signed coal order itself as a winter expense. She checked delivery notes, measured what remained in storage, and estimated what the occupied rooms had actually consumed. The used coal belonged against winter service, with an amount payable to the merchant; unused coal remained inventory. When the bill arrived with a disputed delivery, she recorded the supported amount and kept the difference open instead of forcing certainty into the period.

Spring created the opposite temptation. A festival paid deposits for rooms it would use in summer, while several winter guests still owed money. Cash arrived before one service and after another. The bookkeeper recorded a contract liability for the deposit and receivables for earned winter stays, then revised an estimate when one guest defaulted. When coal cash was finally paid, she reduced cash and the payable without charging the whole winter cost to spring again.

After adjustment, winter was less profitable than first believed, while spring had not suddenly become disastrous. The owner reduced the cellar plan and began recording long-stay guest charges in the months when the rooms were actually used, even before payment arrived.

The revised books also changed a practical decision. Once the owner saw that winter rooms had consumed most of their apparent surplus, he cancelled the full cellar, kept cash for the coal payable, and built only a small rack. When a spring debtor failed, the inn reduced its receivable estimate rather than rewriting the winter occupancy. Better timing did not create cash; it prevented one season from borrowing another season's appearance.

When the final basket of coal entered the stove the next winter, the bookkeeper checked the delivery note, measured the remaining pile, and wrote first on the winter page. She tied the unpaid invoice to the payable ledger and placed the summer deposit in a different folder. The owner counted cash for wages separately before approving even the small wine rack. The merchant's coins still waited until the snow melted.
storyParagraphsZh: 寒冬里，山路旅店向煤商赊来一整仓煤，约定开春结账。客房每天住满，钱箱不断增加。老板只记录实际收付的银钱，于是冬季账面格外漂亮，他还准备把“盈余”拿去扩建酒窖。
春天客人减少，煤商却带来整张账单。钱一付，春季突然出现巨额亏损。老板抱怨春天生意太差，却忘了那笔钱买的是冬天已经烧尽的火。
账房没有把签下煤炭订单就自动当成冬季费用。她核对送货单，量出仓内余煤，再估算住满客房实际烧掉多少。已用煤与冬季服务相配，同时留下应付煤商的义务；未用部分仍是存货。账单里有一车数量争议时，她只确认有证据支持的金额，把差额留待核查，没有为求整齐硬塞进本期。
春天又出现相反诱惑：节庆提前支付夏季订房押金，几名冬客却仍欠房费。现金在一项服务前到达、在另一项服务后才来。账房把押金记作尚待履行的义务，把已赚冬账记成应收；一名住客违约时，再修订估计。煤款真正付出时，她只减少现金和应付，不把冬季费用重复压给春天。
调整以后，冬季没有原先那么赚钱，春季也没有突然变得糟糕。老板因此缩小酒窖计划，并开始把尚未收钱的长期住客费用也记在他们实际住宿的月份。
调整后的账还改变了实际决定。老板看见冬季客房已经耗掉大半表面盈余，便取消整座酒窖，为应付煤款留住现金，只搭一排小酒架。春季一名欠款客人违约时，旅店下调应收估计，没有反过来改写冬季入住事实。更合适的时点不会制造现金，却阻止一个季节借用另一个季节的外表。
第二年最后一筐冬煤入炉时，账房先核送货单，量过仓内余煤，再在冬季那页郑重落下一笔。她把未付账单系在应付账旁，把夏季押金另放一夹；老板又先从现金中留出工资，才批准那排小酒架。煤商的钱仍等到雪化后才付，他看见绳结，没有再把箱中余额叫作盈余。
explanationParagraphs: Accrual accounting recognises rights, obligations, revenue, and expenses when the underlying economic activity occurs rather than only when cash changes hands. Receivables, payables, inventory, deferrals, and estimates allocate effects to relevant periods. Accrual profit therefore differs from cash flow and depends on evidence, standards, and judgement.
explanationParagraphsZh: 权责发生制在经济活动形成权利、义务、收入或费用并满足适当确认条件时记录，而不只在现金交换时记录。应收、应付、存货、递延与估计等项目把影响归入相关期间。权责利润因此不同于现金流，也依赖证据、准则和判断。

articles.title: The Tax That Passed Through the Gate
articles.summary: The gate charges one coin per cart of pottery; the potter pays it, but he is not the only person who receives less.
articles.summaryZh: 城门向每车陶器收一枚税，交钱的是陶商，少拿钱的却不止他一个。
storyParagraphs: The city required pottery merchants to pay one coin for every cart entering the gate. The collector assumed the burden therefore belonged to merchants, because their hands placed the money in his box. After paying the first coin, potter Luoxin raised the price of each jar slightly.

Some customers urgently needed water vessels and paid more. Others bought wooden barrels, so Luoxin could not add the whole tax to prices. He asked the clay yard for a discount and reduced the hours of temporary workers. With no other nearby buyer, the clay yard accepted part of the cut.

The collector compared pottery with a new tax on rare purple dye. Wealthy buyers continued ordering the dye, so its sellers passed much of that charge into price. Pottery buyers could switch to barrels, while Luoxin could delay only some shipments and workers had few nearby employers. The same legal payer did not imply the same final distribution. What mattered was how strongly buyers and sellers changed quantities when their net price changed.

After a month, the tax box still received one coin per cart, but the effects were scattered. Customers paid some through higher prices; Luoxin lost margin; the clay yard accepted a lower price; temporary workers lost days. The collector counted the jars sold before and after rather than merely dividing the coin by four. Those with fewer substitutes, less bargaining power, or less ability to wait had greater difficulty passing the burden elsewhere, and some burden appeared as trades that never occurred.

The following year, a new road allowed the clay yard to sell to another city, and it refused further discounts. The merchant then carried a larger share. The law had not changed, but the burden among the parties had.

The council wanted one number naming who bore the coin. The collector refused false precision. He reported observed price changes, quantities, wages, and margins, then explained that contracts and adjustment time could move the shares again. For bread, where families had fewer substitutes, he recommended a separate distribution review. The legal receipt remained clear; the economic sacrifice required tracing people who never touched the tax box.

When preparing his final report, the collector no longer copied only the payer's name. After the pottery merchant, he added columns for customers, clay yard, workers, and sales that disappeared. In the margin he dated each price, wage, quantity, and margin comparison, because the new road had already shown that substitutes, bargaining, contracts, and adjustment over time could move the burden again.
storyParagraphsZh: 城里规定，每车陶器入门时由陶商缴一枚银币。收税员因此认定负担自然落在陶商身上，因为钱从他们手里进入木箱。陶商罗辛缴完第一枚后，把每只壶的价格略微提高。
有些顾客急需储水罐，只能多付；另一些人改买木桶，罗辛无法把整枚税都加进价格。他转而要求泥场降价，又减少临时工的工时。泥场没有别的近城买家，只好接受一部分降价。
收税员又比较一项稀有紫染料税。富裕买家仍照常订货，染料商便能把大部分税加进价格。陶器顾客却能改买木桶；罗辛只能延后少数货车，临时工在附近也没有多少雇主。法律上的缴款人相同，并不意味着最后分担相同；关键是买卖双方在净价格变化后会多大幅度改变数量。
一个月后，税箱里每车仍只有一枚银币，变化却散在市场各处：顾客通过涨价多付一些，罗辛少赚利润，泥场接受降价，临时工失去工日。收税员比较征税前后卖出的壶数，没有把银币机械地四等分。替代选择少、议价能力弱或无法等待的人更难转移负担；还有一部分税体现在那些最终没有发生的交易里。
第二年，远路开通，泥场能卖给外城，便拒绝继续降价。陶商承担的部分随之增加。法令没有改，实际落在各方身上的份额却变了。
议会要求用一个数字说清谁承担那枚税，收税员拒绝了这种假精确。他报告可观察的价格、数量、工资和利润变化，并注明合同与调整时间还会移动份额。对替代更少的面包，他建议另做分配审查。法律收据很清楚，真实资源损失却必须追到那些从未碰过税箱的人。
收税员整理最终报告时，不再只抄木箱里的法定实际缴款人名字。他在陶商后面又添上顾客、泥场、工人和消失的交易几栏，给价格、工资、数量与利润比较逐一标日期。那条新路已经证明，替代选择、议价、合同与调整时间都可能让税的实际份额再次移动。
explanationParagraphs: Tax incidence asks who ultimately bears a tax through changes in prices, wages, profits, income, or opportunities, which may differ from the person legally required to remit it. The ability of each side to change buying or selling behaviour shapes the burden; the less responsive side often bears more. Time, substitutes, contracts, market power, and institutions also matter.
explanationParagraphsZh: 税负归宿关注谁最终通过价格、工资、利润、收入或机会变化承担税收，可能不同于法律规定的缴税者。各方调整买卖的能力会影响负担分配；通常越难改变行为的一方承担越多。时间、替代品、合同、市场力量和制度也会改变结果。

articles.title: One Hundred Coins After Ten Winters
articles.titleZh: 等待十个冬天的一百枚钱
articles.summary: An employer offers a mill apprentice one hundred coins today or the same one hundred after ten years.
articles.summaryZh: 雇主让磨坊学徒选择今天的一百枚钱，或十年后完全相同的一百枚。
storyParagraphs: When a mill closed, its owner owed apprentice Suining one hundred coins. He offered two choices: payment today, or the same hundred coins after ten winters if she left the money with him. He said the number was identical and waiting would prevent her from spending carelessly.

Suining almost agreed. Yet she could buy a small millstone for one hundred coins and earn money grinding neighbours' grain each year. Waiting would cost not only present spending but also the income the stone might produce. Ten years later, the same hundred coins might not buy the same amount of grain.

Suining asked the town lender for a checkable comparison. At five per cent a year, one hundred coins invested and reinvested would become about one hundred sixty-three after ten winters; conversely, a promise of one hundred then was worth only about sixty-one today at that rate. The lender wrote both calculations beside the contract. The rate was not magic: a safer debtor, inflation, alternative work, liquidity needs, and the purpose of the decision could justify a different one.

She also considered whether the owner would still be trading in ten years and whether she could withdraw early. The mill had already closed, so default risk was not decoration. Longer waiting meant uncertainty and lost access, while an urgent family need made liquidity valuable now. The owner offered one hundred twenty after ten years, still far below the lender's comparison. Suining rejected it, though taking cash meant bearing the risks of her own investment rather than eliminating risk.

Suining chose payment now and bought the stone. During the first winter, its earnings repaired the axle. In the second, it began providing steady income. After ten years, her cash was not guaranteed to be greater, but it had passed through ten years of use and risk.

The stone did not make every year profitable. A drought left it idle, an axle failed, and some earnings were consumed rather than reinvested. Suining kept the original comparison beside the repair bills so that hindsight would not turn an uncertain choice into a guaranteed triumph. When neighbours asked what ten-year promise was fair, she began with dated cash flows and assumptions, not with the largest future number.

She carved the payment date beside the stone and added one short mark after each winter. Beside the drought year, the mark remained shallow; beside the axle repair, she carved its cost. The ten marks preserved both use and risk rather than pretending compounding had followed a smooth road.
storyParagraphsZh: 磨坊关闭时，雇主欠学徒岁宁一百枚钱。他提出两个办法：今天付清，或把钱留在自己手里，十个冬天后再付同样一百枚。雇主说数字完全相同，后一个选择还能避免岁宁现在乱花。
岁宁原本想同意。可她正好能用一百枚买下一块小磨石，每年替邻居磨麦都能收钱。若等待十年，她失去的不只是今天的消费，还包括磨石在这些年可能带来的收入；到那时，一百枚能买到的粮食也未必相同。
岁宁请镇上放贷人做一份可核算比较。按每年百分之五，一百枚若逐年投入并把收益继续投入，十个冬天后约为一百六十三；反过来，十年后的一百枚按此比率折回今天，约值六十一。放贷人把两种算法都写在契约旁。利率不是魔法：债务人可靠程度、通胀、替代工作、流动需要和比较目的不同，适用数字也会改变。
她还考虑雇主十年后是否仍经营、自己能否提前取钱。磨坊已经关闭，违约并非装饰性的担心；等待越长，不确定与失去使用权的代价越大，家里眼下又正需要可动用的钱。雇主改口承诺十年后一百二十枚，仍远低于那份比较。岁宁拒绝了，尽管现在收款只会让她承担自己投资的风险，并不会消除风险。
岁宁最终选择现在收款，买下磨石。第一年冬天，她把赚来的钱用于修轴；第二年，磨石开始稳定带来收入。十年后，她的钱箱并不保证更多，却已经经过十年的使用与风险。
磨石并非年年赚钱：旱季让它闲置，木轴也坏过，有些收入被生活花掉，没有继续投入。岁宁把最初比较与修理账放在一起，不让事后结果把一个有风险的选择改写成必然胜利。邻居再问十年承诺是否公平时，她先列每个日期的现金与假设，而不是先看最大的未来数字。
她在磨石边刻下收款日期，每过一个冬天便添一道短痕；旱灾那年刻痕很浅，换木轴旁还刻着成本。十道痕同时留下使用与风险，没有把复利假装成一条平滑道路。
explanationParagraphs: The time value of money means that equal nominal amounts at different dates are generally not equivalent. Earlier funds can be invested or consumed, while delay involves inflation, default, illiquidity, and postponed opportunity. Present and future value compare dated amounts using a rate suited to the term, risk, alternatives, and purpose.
explanationParagraphsZh: 货币时间价值指不同日期的相同名义金额通常并不等价。较早资金可以投资或消费，等待还涉及通胀、违约、流动性和推迟机会。现值与终值使用适当折现率比较跨期金额；所选利率还应反映期限、风险、替代方案与具体目的。

articles.title: Five Ships Beneath the Same Cloud
articles.summary: A merchant divides his cargo among five ships, believing the risk is spread, then sends them into the same storm.
articles.summaryZh: 商人把货分到五艘船上，以为已经分散风险，却让它们同日驶入同一场风暴。
storyParagraphs: Merchant Baichuan no longer wanted all his spices aboard one vessel. He bought five smaller ships and divided the cargo evenly, telling everyone that even if one sank, four would return. He was indeed no longer dependent on any single ship.

But all five used the same harbour, route, and departure day. When a storm crossed the strait, every vessel was in nearby water. Two were damaged and three returned to port, leaving the entire season's spice undelivered. The number of ships had increased; their shared weather had not decreased.

Baichuan's accountant laid five voyage records across the floor. Separate captains and hulls had reduced failures unique to one vessel, but common port closure, weather, spice prices, lender, and buyer still tied the returns together. Adding a sixth ship to the same route would barely change those connections. Nor would equal cargo automatically be safest: weights had to reflect loss size, volatility, and how each route moved with the others.

The following year, Baichuan divided departures across months and routes, sent part of the cargo overland, used different warehouses and buyers, and traded some goods affected by other seasons. He limited any one exposure rather than counting vessels. This increased fees, slowed oversight, and meant declining the route with the highest expected profit. His partners threatened to leave, so he accepted a smaller personal share to fund the first year's extra management.

An autumn storm delayed two southern vessels while the overland goods arrived. Later, a mountain closure interrupted the road, and a northern ship supplied the market. Losses did not disappear, but they no longer occurred together every time.

Then a regional war closed sea lanes and mountain roads together. Nearly every position suffered, revealing a common shock no arrangement could remove. Baichuan kept emergency cash and reduced total cargo rather than claiming another asset would always offset the loss. Diversifying had changed the pattern of ordinary setbacks; it had not repealed crisis, correlation shifts, or the cost of being wrong about hidden links.

When carefully redrawing the fleet plan, Baichuan did not write only the number of ships. He varied the thickness of each route by cargo weight and drew lines connecting shared ports, seasons, lenders, and buyers. In red he marked the war closure crossing every route, then tested repeatedly on paper how much loss the remaining cash could absorb before payments failed across the whole trading season. He set a sealed reserve beside the map rather than drawing a fictitious escape line or counting another vessel.
storyParagraphsZh: 商人柏川不愿再把全部香料装在一艘船上。他买下五艘小船，把货平均分开，逢人便说即使沉掉一艘，另外四艘也会回来。他确实不再依赖任何一条船。
可是五艘船使用同一港口、同一航道，也在同一天出发。海峡风暴来临时，它们全部停在相近水域。两艘受损，三艘返航，整季香料仍未能送达。船的数量增加了，共同面对的天气却没有减少。
账房把五次航行记录铺满地面。不同船长和船体确实减少了单船特有故障，港口关闭、海峡天气、香料价格、贷款人和买家却仍把收益绑在一起。再添一艘同路线船，几乎不改变这些连接；平均分货也不自动最稳，权重还要看损失大小、波动以及各路线是否同涨同跌。
第二年，柏川把货分到不同月份与航道，一部分走陆路，另用不同仓库和买家，还经营受其他季节影响的货。他限制任何单项份额，不再只数船。额外安排增加费用、拖慢监督，也迫使他放弃预期利润最高的路线。合伙人扬言退出，他只得少分自己的收益，先支付第一年新增管理成本。
秋天，南海风暴使两艘船延误，陆路货物却已到达；随后山路封闭，北线船又补上供应。并非每项损失都消失，只是它们不再总在同一时刻发生。
后来区域战争同时封闭海路与山道，几乎所有安排一同受损，暴露出无法靠组合消掉的共同冲击。柏川保留应急现金并减少总货量，没有声称总有另一项资产能抵消损失。分开安排改变了日常挫折的组合，却没有废除危机、相关性突变或误判隐藏连接的代价。
柏川重新铺纸画船队图时，不再只写船数。他按货物权重画出粗细不同的路线，再连起共享港口、季节、贷款人和买家。最后，他用红笔标出同时穿过所有路线的战争封锁，试算余下现金究竟能承受多少损失，再把封存钱箱放在图旁，没有画一条不存在的逃生路线，也没有再数一艘新船。
explanationParagraphs: Diversification combines exposures whose returns are not perfectly correlated, allowing some individual losses to be offset by other gains. Portfolio risk depends on weights, volatility, and co-movement rather than the number of holdings alone. Diversification can reduce idiosyncratic risk but not common shocks; hidden dependencies, costs, and changing correlations still matter.
explanationParagraphsZh: 分散化把相关性不完全的风险敞口组合，使部分个别损失可能被其他收益抵消。风险取决于权重、波动和共同变化，而非项目数量本身。它可降低特有风险，却不能消除影响所有项目的共同冲击；隐藏依赖、成本与相关性变化仍需检查。

articles.title: The Night Watch After the Policy Was Signed
articles.titleZh: 保单签下以后的守夜人
articles.summary: After insuring the warehouse, its owner does not plan a fire but begins to think one fewer patrol will not matter.
articles.summaryZh: 仓库投保后，老板没有打算纵火，却开始觉得少巡一次夜也没什么。
storyParagraphs: Fire was the cotton warehouse's greatest fear. After owner Xu Cheng purchased full insurance, one accident would no longer destroy his entire property. The renewal was expensive, so he reduced two night guards to one and delayed replacing old lamp wiring, reasoning that a real loss would now be repaid.

The remaining guard was not lazy, but could not inspect both yards at once. One night, the rear wiring sparked and burned three stacks of cotton. The insurer paid as promised and the warehouse continued trading. Xu Cheng had not intended the fire.

The insurer compared records from before and after the policy. Guard hours and maintenance spending had fallen only after coverage began; this was different from discovering before signing that Xu Cheng secretly owned a dangerous warehouse. Protection had changed action that the insurer could not watch every night. The change did not prove wicked intent: each saved patrol looked small to Xu Cheng, while the added chance of loss was shared with someone else.

The following year, the insurer proposed a higher premium, a deductible that left the first loss with the warehouse, verified inspections, and a subsidy for safer wiring. Xu Cheng objected that constant monitoring would turn protection into punishment. They rejected an always-present inspector and instead used periodic checks, gatehouse records, and lower renewal prices after sustained prevention. Xu Cheng paid for the second guard himself and lost the cheapest policy, but retained cover against a fire large enough to ruin the firm.

The arrangement did not return all risk to Xu Cheng or require the insurer to observe every night. Two guards resumed alternating rounds, with inspection records kept at the gatehouse. Protection remained, while behaviour under protection again carried consequences.

The insurer reviewed the arrangement after six months. Patrols had resumed and wiring faults fell, but a guard had skipped one round to help an injured worker; the contract did not punish that judgment. Xu Cheng accepted that no clause could specify every useful action. The goal was to keep prevention worth doing while preserving protection for losses no prudent warehouse could fully avoid.

After his first circuit of the rear yard, the guard signed the record, noted a loose fitting for morning repair, and ran a hand beside the newly replaced wire without touching it. Xu Cheng countersigned the maintenance order, restored the second guard's next shift, and placed the deductible reserve in a separate cash drawer. The insurer would inspect the repair, not every human choice. The policy remained in the gatehouse, no longer mistaken for a patrol.
storyParagraphsZh: 棉仓每年最怕失火。老板许澄买下全额保单后，终于不必一次事故便失去全部家产。续约费用不低，他便把两名守夜人减为一名，又推迟更换老化灯线，认为真正的损失反正有人赔付。
剩下的守夜人并不懒，却无法同时巡视前后两院。一天夜里，后院灯线冒出火星，烧坏了三垛棉。保险商按约赔偿，仓库得以继续经营，许澄也没有故意制造事故。
保险商比较投保前后的记录，发现守夜工时与维护支出都在保障生效后下降。这与签约前才发现许澄暗藏一座危险仓库不同：保护改变了保险商无法逐夜观察的行动。变化也不证明他怀有恶意；每少巡一圈，在许澄眼里只节省一点钱，增加的失火后果却会与别人共同承担。
第二年，保险商提出提高保费、由仓库自担最初损失、核验检查，并补贴更安全的灯线。许澄反对全天监督，因为那会把保障变成惩罚。双方放弃常驻检查员，改用定期抽查、门房记录和持续预防后的续保降价。许澄自费恢复第二名守夜人，也失去了最低保费，却仍保留足以避免企业被大火摧毁的保障。
新安排没有把风险全部推回许澄，也没有要求保险商观察每个夜晚。仓库恢复两人轮班，检查记录留在门房。保护仍在，受保护后的行为也重新有了后果。
六个月后，保险商复查安排。巡逻恢复，灯线故障减少；一名守夜人却曾为帮助受伤工人漏掉一圈，合同没有惩罚这种判断。许澄接受没有条款能写尽所有有益行动。安排要让预防仍值得做，也要为谨慎仓库无法完全避免的大损失保留保障。
第一次巡完后院，守夜人在记录簿上签名，注明一处松动接头留待早晨维修，又把手停在新灯线旁，没有碰它。许澄复签维修单，恢复第二名守夜人的下个班次，再把免赔准备金单独放进钱箱。保险商会查维修，不会监视每个选择。保单仍挂在门房，却再也没有被当成一次巡逻。
explanationParagraphs: Moral hazard occurs when protection from part of a consequence changes behaviour that is difficult to observe or specify completely in a contract. It is an incentive and information problem and need not involve malicious intent. Deductibles, shared loss, monitoring, experience-based pricing, and prevention support can reduce it, but may also weaken protection or impose excessive surveillance.
explanationParagraphsZh: 道德风险发生在某人受到部分后果保护后，其难以被完整观察或写入合同的行为随之改变。它是激励与信息问题，不必包含恶意。免赔、共同承担、监督、经验费率和预防支持可以缓解，但也需避免保障过弱、过度监控或阻碍有益行动。
